views.name: orders_enriched_times
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_status,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_approved_at,
  order_delivered_carrier_date,
  order_delivered_customer_date,
  order_estimated_delivery_date,
  -- parsed as ISO8601 text (SQLite will accept original if already ISO-like); keep originals too
  CASE WHEN order_purchase_timestamp = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_purchase_timestamp END AS order_purchase_timestamp_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_approved_at = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_approved_at END AS order_approved_at_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_delivered_carrier_date = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_carrier_date END AS order_delivered_carrier_date_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_customer_date END AS order_delivered_customer_date_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_estimated_delivery_date = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_estimated_delivery_date END AS order_estimated_delivery_date_normalized,
  -- derived: delivery latency in seconds where timestamps available (NULL-safe)
  CASE
    WHEN order_approved_at IS NOT NULL AND order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND order_approved_at <> '' AND order_purchase_timestamp <> ''
    THEN (strftime('%s', order_approved_at) - strftime('%s', order_purchase_timestamp))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS approval_lag_seconds,
  CASE
    WHEN order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND order_delivered_customer_date <> '' AND order_purchase_timestamp <> ''
    THEN (strftime('%s', order_delivered_customer_date) - strftime('%s', order_purchase_timestamp))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS purchase_to_delivery_seconds,
  CASE
    WHEN order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL AND order_delivered_customer_date <> '' AND order_estimated_delivery_date <> ''
    THEN (strftime('%s', order_delivered_customer_date) - strftime('%s', order_estimated_delivery_date))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS delivery_vs_estimate_seconds
FROM orders

params.description: One-row-per-order enrichment of orders with normalized timestamp text fields and common delivery/approval latency metrics in seconds.
params.when_to_use: Report or analytical query at the order grain (one row per order) that needs order timestamps, normalized timestamp text, or order-level latency measures (approval lag, purchase-to-delivery, delivery vs estimate). | As a base for joining order-level attributes to other order-level aggregates (payments, order-level financials, seller-by-order metrics) without duplicating measures. | When composing time-based sequence or SLA analyses per order (e.g., distribution of approval times, on-time delivery rate) where timestamps may be empty strings and should be treated as NULL.
params.output_schema: order_id: unique identifier for the order; selected directly from orders.order_id | customer_id: identifier of the customer who placed the order; selected directly from orders.customer_id | order_status: order lifecycle status (e.g., delivered, shipped); selected directly from orders.order_status | order_purchase_timestamp: original purchase timestamp text as stored; selected directly from orders.order_purchase_timestamp | order_approved_at: original approval timestamp text as stored; selected directly from orders.order_approved_at | order_delivered_carrier_date: original carrier delivery date timestamp text as stored; selected directly from orders.order_delivered_carrier_date | order_delivered_customer_date: original delivered to customer timestamp text as stored; selected directly from orders.order_delivered_customer_date | order_estimated_delivery_date: original estimated delivery date timestamp text as stored; selected directly from orders.order_estimated_delivery_date | order_purchase_timestamp_normalized: equals order_purchase_timestamp except empty-string -> NULL; derived from orders.order_purchase_timestamp | order_approved_at_normalized: equals order_approved_at except empty-string -> NULL; derived from orders.order_approved_at | order_delivered_carrier_date_normalized: equals order_delivered_carrier_date except empty-string -> NULL; derived from orders.order_delivered_carrier_date | order_delivered_customer_date_normalized: equals order_delivered_customer_date except empty-string -> NULL; derived from orders.order_delivered_customer_date | order_estimated_delivery_date_normalized: equals order_estimated_delivery_date except empty-string -> NULL; derived from orders.order_estimated_delivery_date | approval_lag_seconds: seconds difference (order_approved_at - order_purchase_timestamp) when both timestamps are present and non-empty; computed via strftime('%s', order_approved_at) - strftime('%s', order_purchase_timestamp) | purchase_to_delivery_seconds: seconds difference (order_delivered_customer_date - order_purchase_timestamp) when both timestamps are present and non-empty; computed via strftime('%s', order_delivered_customer_date) - strftime('%s', order_purchase_timestamp) | delivery_vs_estimate_seconds: seconds difference (order_delivered_customer_date - order_estimated_delivery_date) when both timestamps are present and non-empty; computed via strftime('%s', order_delivered_customer_date) - strftime('%s', order_estimated_delivery_date)
params.grounded_columns: orders.order_id | orders.customer_id | orders.order_status | orders.order_purchase_timestamp | orders.order_approved_at | orders.order_delivered_carrier_date | orders.order_delivered_customer_date | orders.order_estimated_delivery_date
params.metric: approval_lag_seconds = CASE WHEN order_approved_at IS NOT NULL AND order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND order_approved_at <> '' AND order_purchase_timestamp <> '' THEN (strftime('%s', order_approved_at) - strftime('%s', order_purchase_timestamp)) ELSE NULL END | purchase_to_delivery_seconds = CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND order_delivered_customer_date <> '' AND order_purchase_timestamp <> '' THEN (strftime('%s', order_delivered_customer_date) - strftime('%s', order_purchase_timestamp)) ELSE NULL END | delivery_vs_estimate_seconds = CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL AND order_delivered_customer_date <> '' AND order_estimated_delivery_date <> '' THEN (strftime('%s', order_delivered_customer_date) - strftime('%s', order_estimated_delivery_date)) ELSE NULL END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to AGG or one-row-per-order views/tables on order_id — safe because orders_enriched_times is one-row-per-order so joining to another one-row-per-order dataset preserves row cardinality. Example safe joins: join to order_payments_agg_by_order on order_id (order_payments_agg_by_order is an aggregate keyed by order_id, one row per order) — measures from both sides are not duplicated. | Safe to join to order_items_financials on order_id only if that view is guaranteed to be one-row-per-order; if order_items_financials is aggregated to order_id (one row per order) the join is safe. If order_items_financials is at order_item granularity (multiple rows per order) do NOT join directly without re-aggregation because that will multiply orders_enriched_times rows and duplicate per-order measures. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail tables or views (for example, order_items_by_product if it is one-to-many per order, orders_with_customer_location if it contains multiple locations per order) without first aggregating the detail side to order_id. Directly joining a many-side will multiply this view's rows and incorrectly duplicate order-level metrics. | When composing with JOIN-type sibling views listed as JOIN (orders_with_payments_items, orders_with_customer_location), inspect their grain: if they are already one-row-per-order the join is safe; if they are multi-row per order they must be reduced to one row per order (e.g., SUM/AVG of measures or choose first) before joining. | When building higher-level aggregates (e.g., total approval_lag_seconds across customers), aggregate approval_lag_seconds after joining; do not sum approval_lag_seconds then join to a many-side which would replicate rows. Prefer: aggregate the many-side to order-level first, then join to this view, then aggregate to customer or higher grain.

views.description: Normalize orders timestamps into ISO8601 and expose delivery lag measures. Use when analyzing time-to-approve / time-to-deliver metrics or joining orders by normalized timestamps. | Use for: Calculate average time-to-approve orders; Compute delivery lateness vs estimate; Filter orders by purchase or delivery time windows; Correlate delivery speed with review scores or customer attributes

views.name: order_items_financials
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_item_id,
  product_id,
  seller_id,
  shipping_limit_date,
  price,
  freight_value,
  -- derived total charged for the item
  (COALESCE(price, 0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value, 0.0)) AS item_total_value
FROM order_items

params.description: Provides per-order-item financial details (price, freight, and item total) for each order_item row.
params.when_to_use: Calculate revenue or charges at the individual order_item grain (e.g., item-level invoicing, item-level revenue reports). | Compose item-level financials into order-level or product-level aggregates by summing item_total_value, price, or freight_value. | Join item financials to product, seller, or order dimensions when you need monetary values tied to specific order_item rows.
params.output_schema: order_id: identifier of the order containing the item; sourced from order_items.order_id | order_item_id: identifier of the specific item within the order (row-level grain); sourced from order_items.order_item_id | product_id: identifier of the product on this order item; sourced from order_items.product_id | seller_id: identifier of the seller for this item; sourced from order_items.seller_id | shipping_limit_date: the order item's shipping limit date (expected latest ship date); sourced from order_items.shipping_limit_date | price: the unit/charged price for this order item; sourced from order_items.price | freight_value: the freight/shipping cost charged for this order item; sourced from order_items.freight_value | item_total_value: derived total charged for the order item, defined as COALESCE(price, 0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value, 0.0)
params.grounded_columns: order_items.order_id | order_items.order_item_id | order_items.product_id | order_items.seller_id | order_items.shipping_limit_date | order_items.price | order_items.freight_value
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to product_catalog_with_translation on product_id — safe because product_catalog_with_translation is a product-level dimension (one row per product_id) so joining will not duplicate order_item rows or their monetary measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to seller_performance_by_order on (order_id, seller_id) only if seller_performance_by_order is guaranteed one-row-per-(order_id, seller_id); safe because measures in this view are at order_item grain and will not be duplicated when matched to a single row per (order_id, seller_id). | cardinality-SAFE: join to orders_enriched_times or orders_with_customer_location on order_id — safe when those views are one-row-per-order (order_id) dimensions, because each order_item maps to exactly one order row and item measures are not multiplied. | NOT SAFE WITHOUT RE-AGGREGATION: do NOT directly join to order_payments_agg_by_order (AGG) and then treat item_total_value as aggregated without aligning grain — while order_payments_agg_by_order is likely one-row-per-order (order_id) and can be safely joined, caution is required if the target agg produces multiple rows per order (e.g., partitioned by payment_type) because that would duplicate item rows. If joining to a payments table that is one-to-many (multiple payment rows per order), first aggregate payments to one-row-per-order before joining. | NOT SAFE WITHOUT RE-AGGREGATION: do NOT join to order_items_by_product (AGG) or any other one-to-many aggregate keyed at product_id or seller_id that expands rows per order_item — these will duplicate item-level measures. Instead, either aggregate this view up to the same grain (e.g., sum item_total_value by product_id) before joining, or aggregate the other side to one row per key. | NOT SAFE WITHOUT RE-AGGREGATION: do NOT join to sibling detail-level tables that are one-to-many with respect to order_item (for example, line-level adjustments, promotions, or multiple shipment attempts per order_item) without first deciding the desired aggregation. Joining such one-to-many tables directly will multiply item_total_value and distort sums. | general guidance: when composing into higher-level metrics (order- or product-level), aggregate (SUM) price, freight_value, and item_total_value from this view at the desired grain before joining to other one-row-per-key dimensions. When joining to any view/table, verify the join keys correspond to a one-to-one or many-to-one relationship from this view's grain (order_id, order_item_id) to the other side to ensure measures are not duplicated.

views.description: Clean and expose per-order-item financials (price, freight, and total). Use as the canonical per-item monetary row for aggregations or joins to products/sellers/orders. | Use for: Aggregate sales or freight by order or seller; Find most valuable items or orders by sum of item_total_value; Compute average item price or freight by product category or seller

views.name: order_payments_agg_by_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_attempts_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(payment_value, 0.0)) AS payment_total_value,
  MIN(payment_type) AS any_payment_type_sample,
  MAX(payment_installments) AS max_payment_installments
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY order_id

params.description: Per-order aggregation of payment activity: counts, total value, a sample payment type and the maximum installments for payments attached to each order.
params.when_to_use: Return one-row-per-order payment summaries (e.g., show payment count and total for each order). | Join payment-level aggregates to order-level dimensions (customer, order date, seller) without duplicating payment measures. | Compose further aggregations by order (e.g., compute revenue per order bucket) or join to order_items to compute order-level metrics that combine items and payments (with care). | Filter orders by payment characteristics (e.g., orders with >1 payment attempt or max_installments >= N).
params.output_schema: order_id: the primary key of the order for which payments are aggregated; derived from order_payments.order_id (GROUP BY column). | payment_attempts_count: number of payment attempt rows for this order; derived from COUNT(*) over order_payments grouped by order_id. | payment_total_value: sum of payment_value for this order with NULLs treated as 0.0; derived from SUM(COALESCE(order_payments.payment_value, 0.0)). | any_payment_type_sample: a deterministic sample of payment_type for the order implemented as MIN(payment_type); derived from MIN(order_payments.payment_type). | max_payment_installments: maximum payment_installments observed for the order; derived from MAX(order_payments.payment_installments).
params.metric: payment_attempts_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of order_payments rows per order_id | payment_total_value = SUM(COALESCE(payment_value, 0.0))  -- total payment value per order, NULLs treated as 0 | any_payment_type_sample = MIN(payment_type)  -- deterministic sample; not necessarily representative when multiple types exist | max_payment_installments = MAX(payment_installments)  -- largest installments value across payments for the order
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_enriched_times (NORM) on order_id — safe because orders_enriched_times is one-row-per-order, so joining preserves one-row-per-order and does not duplicate this view's measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_latest_order_rank (RANK) on order_id — safe when that view is one-row-per-order; ensures measures remain at order-grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to seller_performance_by_order (AGG) on order_id — safe if that sibling AGG is also one-row-per-order; both sides remain one-row-per-order and measures are not duplicated. | do NOT join directly to order_items_financials (NORM) or order_items_by_product (AGG) without re-aggregation — these are one-to-many with order (multiple items per order); joining would multiply payment_attempts_count and payment_total_value unless you re-aggregate (e.g., SUM(payment_total_value) AFTER grouping by order) or join on pre-aggregated, one-row-per-order results. | do NOT join directly to product_catalog_with_translation or any product-level table on product_id unless you first aggregate items to order-level — product tables are many-to-one from items but order-items is many-per-order, so joining through items will duplicate order-level payment measures. | when combining with orders_with_payments_items or orders_with_customer_location (JOINs): confirm those views are one-row-per-order. If they are one-row-per-order, joining is safe; if they expand orders to multiple rows (e.g., one row per item or per payment), re-aggregate the expanded side back to order grain before joining or use this view as the aggregated side and join dimension tables only. | general planner rule: this view is strictly one-row-per-order (grain = order_id). Any join partner that is also one-row-per-order keeps measures stable. Any join partner that is one-to-many from order will duplicate these measures and therefore requires re-aggregation of the many-side or using this view as the aggregated side in a higher-level aggregation.

views.description: Aggregate payments to the order level: total paid, number of installments records, and count of payment attempts. Use when comparing paid value to order item totals or computing payment-method mixes per order. | Use for: Compare paid amount to order items total; Segment orders by payment type or installment counts; Detect incomplete payments (payment_total_value < items total)

views.name: order_items_by_product
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  COUNT(*) AS items_sold_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0)) AS revenue_price_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS revenue_freight_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS revenue_total_value
FROM order_items
GROUP BY product_id

params.description: Aggregated sales metrics per product: counts of items sold and summed revenue (price, freight, total).
params.when_to_use: Get total items sold and revenue measures for a specific product_id or set of product_ids. | Build product-level revenue or sales reports and dashboards. | Join product-level metrics to product dimension data (e.g., product catalog) without re-aggregation. | Compose into higher-level aggregations (e.g., category or seller) by re-aggregating this view's outputs.
params.output_schema: product_id: identifier of the product for which the aggregates are computed; derived from order_items.product_id | items_sold_count: integer count of order_items rows for the product (COUNT(*)); derived from COUNT(*) over order_items grouped by product_id | revenue_price_sum: sum of price for the product (treating NULL as 0.0) ; derived from SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price, 0.0)) | revenue_freight_sum: sum of freight_value for the product (treating NULL as 0.0); derived from SUM(COALESCE(order_items.freight_value, 0.0)) | revenue_total_value: sum of (price + freight_value) for the product (each NULL treated as 0.0); derived from SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price,0.0) + COALESCE(order_items.freight_value,0.0))
params.metric: items_sold_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of order_items rows per product_id | revenue_price_sum = SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price, 0.0)) | revenue_freight_sum = SUM(COALESCE(order_items.freight_value, 0.0)) | revenue_total_value = SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price,0.0) + COALESCE(order_items.freight_value,0.0))
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_catalog_with_translation on product_id — safe because this view is one row per product_id, so joining enriches product attributes without duplicating the view's measures (product_catalog_with_translation must be one-row-per-product_id). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to seller_performance_by_order or order_payments_agg_by_order is NOT safe directly on order or order_id because those are at order-level (one-to-many relative to this product-level view) and the join would duplicate measures; instead, join through an order-level aggregated view that has been reduced to product_id or re-aggregate after the join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: to produce category-level metrics, aggregate this view by category after joining to product_catalog_with_translation (GROUP BY category_id SUM(revenue_total_value), SUM(items_sold_count)). Re-aggregate to avoid double-counting. | do NOT join to orders_enriched_times, orders_with_payments_items, orders_with_customer_location, or any orders/order_items level JOIN that contains multiple rows per product_id without re-aggregation first — these are one-to-many towards this product grain and will multiply items_sold_count and revenue measures. | when composing into larger queries that combine multiple measures (e.g., seller or customer rollups), prefer: (a) join this view to strictly one-row-per-product dimensions, or (b) join raw order_items and re-compute aggregates at the desired grain. If joining to multi-row tables, use SUM(...) with grouping on product_id (or target grain) to re-aggregate and preserve correctness.

views.description: Aggregate item-level metrics grouped by product: number of times sold, total revenue (price), total freight and total item value. Use for product performance and top-seller analyses. | Use for: Top-selling products by units or revenue; Revenue contribution by product; Join with product attributes for category-level reporting

views.name: orders_with_payments_items
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  oi.items_count,
  oi.items_price_sum,
  oi.items_freight_sum,
  oi.items_total_value,
  p.payment_attempts_count,
  p.payment_total_value
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) AS items_count,
    SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0)) AS items_price_sum,
    SUM(COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS items_freight_sum,
    SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS items_total_value
  FROM order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) AS payment_attempts_count,
    SUM(COALESCE(payment_value,0.0)) AS payment_total_value
  FROM order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
) p ON o.order_id = p.order_id

params.description: Per-order rollup that returns one row per order with basic order attributes plus aggregated item and payment metrics.
params.when_to_use: Report total items, item-based money and freight, and payment totals per order. | Filter or group orders by customer, status, or purchase timestamp while retaining aggregated item and payment measures. | As an aggregated order-level input when composing higher-level metrics (e.g., customer lifetime value, order-level revenue) without re-aggregating order_items or order_payments manually.
params.output_schema: order_id: Unique identifier of the order. Derived directly from orders.order_id (base table). | customer_id: Customer identifier who placed the order. Derived directly from orders.customer_id (base table). | order_status: Status of the order (as stored in orders.order_status). Derived directly from orders.order_status (base table). | order_purchase_timestamp: Timestamp when the order was placed (orders.order_purchase_timestamp). Derived directly from orders.order_purchase_timestamp (base table). | items_count: Number of order_items rows for this order. Derived from COUNT(*) in the subquery over order_items grouped by order_id (order_items → COUNT(*)). | items_price_sum: Sum of item price for this order. Derived from SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price, 0.0)). | items_freight_sum: Sum of freight_value for this order. Derived from SUM(COALESCE(order_items.freight_value, 0.0)). | items_total_value: Sum of (price + freight_value) for this order. Derived from SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price,0.0) + COALESCE(order_items.freight_value,0.0)). | payment_attempts_count: Number of payment attempts/rows for this order. Derived from COUNT(*) in the subquery over order_payments grouped by order_id (order_payments → COUNT(*)). | payment_total_value: Sum of payment_value for this order. Derived from SUM(COALESCE(order_payments.payment_value, 0.0)).
params.grounded_columns: orders.order_id | orders.customer_id | orders.order_status | orders.order_purchase_timestamp | order_items.order_id | order_items.price | order_items.freight_value | order_payments.order_id | order_payments.payment_value
params.metric: items_count = COUNT(order_items.*) grouped by order_id (implemented as COUNT(*) in the order_items aggregation subquery). | items_price_sum = SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price, 0.0)) grouped by order_id. | items_freight_sum = SUM(COALESCE(order_items.freight_value, 0.0)) grouped by order_id. | items_total_value = SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price,0.0) + COALESCE(order_items.freight_value,0.0)) grouped by order_id. | payment_attempts_count = COUNT(order_payments.*) grouped by order_id (implemented as COUNT(*) in the order_payments aggregation subquery). | payment_total_value = SUM(COALESCE(order_payments.payment_value, 0.0)) grouped by order_id.
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do not duplicate measures): join to dimensional/lookups that are one-row-per-key using the keys below. Example safe joins: |  - Join to orders_enriched_times ON order_id = orders_enriched_times.order_id — safe because orders_enriched_times is normalized per order (NORM) and is one-row-per-order, so items_*/payment_* measures are not duplicated. |  - Join to orders_with_customer_location ON order_id = orders_with_customer_location.order_id — safe if that view is one-row-per-order (JOIN sibling indicates it is per-order), so measures stay intact. |  - Join to customer_latest_order_rank ON customer_id = customer_latest_order_rank.customer_id — safe only if customer_latest_order_rank is one-row-per-customer; it will not duplicate per-order measures when joined on customer_id (it attaches customer-level attributes). | Unsafe joins (will duplicate aggregated measures unless you re-aggregate or pre-aggregate the other side): |  - Do NOT directly join to order_items (base table) on order_id without re-aggregating, because order_items is one-to-many relative to this view; joining will multiply this view's item/payment aggregates by the number of matching order_items rows. |  - Do NOT directly join to order_payments (base table) on order_id without re-aggregating, because order_payments is one-to-many and will multiply payment and item aggregates. |  - Do NOT join to sibling views that are aggregated at a finer-than-order grain (e.g., order_items_by_product which is AGG at order_id × product) without re-aggregation on order_id first, because that will duplicate order-level measures. | Guidance for safe composition patterns: |  - If you need to enrich this view with any one-to-many detail (products, item-level attributes, multiple payment attempts detail), first aggregate that detail to order_id (one row per order) and then join to this view on order_id. For example, use order_items_financials or order_payments_agg_by_order (both AGG per order) and join on order_id — safe because those are pre-aggregated to order-level. |  - If you need to produce higher-level aggregates (e.g., customer totals) from this view, GROUP BY customer_id (or other desired key) and SUM the measure columns (items_price_sum, items_freight_sum, items_total_value, payment_total_value) — do not join raw child tables before grouping. |  - When joining on customer_id to a customer-level dimension, ensure the dimension is one-row-per-customer; otherwise aggregate the dimension to one-row-per-customer first.

views.description: Denormalized order-level view joining orders, aggregated payments, and aggregated order items sums. Use when you need a single row per order with totals from items and payments for reconciliation or order-level analytics. | Use for: Find orders with mismatched payment vs items totals; Compute average order value and payment coverage; Filter orders by totals for downstream cohorting

views.name: product_catalog_with_translation
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  t.product_category_name_english,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t
  ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name

params.description: A normalized product-level catalog that provides product attributes and an English translation of the product category, at one row per product_id.
params.when_to_use: Lookup product attributes (dimensions) by product_id for reporting or joining into order-level analyses. | Enrich order-line or sales analyses with product category (original and English), physical attributes (weight, dimensions), and simple content measures (name/description lengths, photo count). | Build aggregated product-level metrics (e.g., average weight by category) by grouping this view's rows.
params.output_schema: product_id: unique identifier for the product; derived directly from products.product_id. | product_category_name: category label as stored in the products table; derived from products.product_category_name. | product_category_name_english: category label translated to English when available; derived from product_category_name_translation.product_category_name_english (LEFT JOIN may yield NULL when no translation exists). | product_name_lenght: integer length of the product name as stored; derived from products.product_name_lenght. | product_description_lenght: integer length of the product description as stored; derived from products.product_description_lenght. | product_photos_qty: count of photos associated with the product as stored; derived from products.product_photos_qty. | product_weight_g: product weight in grams as stored; derived from products.product_weight_g. | product_length_cm: product length in centimeters as stored; derived from products.product_length_cm. | product_height_cm: product height in centimeters as stored; derived from products.product_height_cm. | product_width_cm: product width in centimeters as stored; derived from products.product_width_cm.
params.grounded_columns: products.product_id | products.product_category_name | product_category_name_translation.product_category_name_english | products.product_name_lenght | products.product_description_lenght | products.product_photos_qty | products.product_weight_g | products.product_length_cm | products.product_height_cm | products.product_width_cm
params.metric: product_id = products.product_id | product_category_name = products.product_category_name | product_category_name_english = product_category_name_translation.product_category_name_english (nullable due to LEFT JOIN) | product_name_lenght = products.product_name_lenght | product_description_lenght = products.product_description_lenght | product_photos_qty = products.product_photos_qty | product_weight_g = products.product_weight_g | product_length_cm = products.product_length_cm | product_height_cm = products.product_height_cm | product_width_cm = products.product_width_cm
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to order_items_by_product (AGG) on product_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-product_id and order_items_by_product is pre-aggregated by product_id, so measures will not be duplicated when matching on product_id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_enriched_times (NORM) or order_items_financials (NORM) only by first joining those tables/views on their product_id-keyed aggregate (e.g., order_items_by_product) or by aggregating the NORM tables to product_id before joining — because orders_enriched_times and order_items_financials are normalized/many-to-one relative to products and a direct join would multiply product rows. | do NOT join directly to orders_with_payments_items or order_items_financials (NORM) on product_id without aggregation because those are one-to-many from product -> order_item; a direct join will duplicate product-level measures (e.g., product_photos_qty, product_weight_g). Instead, aggregate the order-side table to product_id (sum/count/metrics) then join. | do NOT join directly to order_payments_agg_by_order on non-order key relationships; join only via order-level keys and ensure aggregation is done at the intended grain. Order_payments_agg_by_order is aggregated by order_id and joining it directly to this product-level view without an order dimension will cause duplication if expanded. | safe to join to dimension-like, one-row-per-key views (e.g., geolocation_zip_centroids) only when joining on their key fields (zipcode etc.) that are one-to-one; this view itself has no geolocation columns so any join there must be via an intermediate key and preserve cardinality by aggregating order-level data first. | general rule: this view's rows are one per products.product_id. Any join to a table/view that is many-to-one (many rows per product_id) will multiply product attributes unless the other side is pre-aggregated to product_id or joined via a one-to-one relationship. When composing, ensure you either aggregate the many-side to product_id or join only to one-row-per-product_id artifacts.

views.description: Product dimension enriched with category translation (English). Use when reporting product attributes with human-readable category labels. | Use for: Report product attributes with translated category labels; Group product-level metrics by English category; Filter products by size/weight thresholds

views.name: customer_latest_order_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_status,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_purchase_timestamp DESC) AS order_rank_per_customer
FROM orders

params.description: Provides each order with its rank (most recent = 1) within its customer by purchase timestamp — answers questions about recency/position of orders per customer.
params.when_to_use: Find the most recent (or Nth most recent) order(s) per customer | Filter orders to customers' latest order(s) (order_rank_per_customer = 1) | Compose time-based retention, churn or recency analyses that need to identify an order's position within a customer's order history | Join latest-order-per-customer to payment, items, product, seller or location data while preserving correct cardinality when taking only rank=1
params.output_schema: order_id: unique identifier of the order — derives from orders.order_id | customer_id: identifier of the customer who placed the order — derives from orders.customer_id | order_purchase_timestamp: timestamp when the order was purchased — derives from orders.order_purchase_timestamp | order_status: status of the order (e.g., delivered, canceled) — derives from orders.order_status | order_rank_per_customer: rank (1 = most recent) of this order among orders for the same customer ordered by order_purchase_timestamp desc — derived by RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_purchase_timestamp DESC)
params.metric: order_rank_per_customer = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY orders.customer_id ORDER BY orders.order_purchase_timestamp DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimension or entity that is one-row-per-order on order_id (for example, order_payments_agg_by_order on order_id) — safe because customer_latest_order_rank is one-row-per-order_id (the view's declared grain), so joining by order_id does NOT duplicate rows or its rank measure. | cardinality-SAFE: join to orders_enriched_times (if it is one-row-per-order_id) on order_id — safe for the same reason (preserves one-row-per-order_id). | cardinality-SAFE: filter this view to order_rank_per_customer = 1 to produce one-row-per-customer, then join to customer- or customer-level views/dimensions (e.g., orders_with_customer_location if it is one-row-per-customer) — safe because the filtered set becomes one-row-per-customer. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed only by order_id (for example, order_items_by_product or order_items_financials) without aggregation: those are one-to-many relative to order_id and will multiply this view's rows/measures. Instead, either (a) aggregate the items/payments to order-level first (e.g., order_items_financials which is AGG by order) and then join on order_id, or (b) if you must join to detail-level items, re-aggregate after the join so metrics are not duplicated. | do NOT join to any view keyed by customer_id that is multi-row-per-customer (for example raw orders or any order-level sibling) without first reducing cardinality (e.g., by filtering to order_rank_per_customer = 1 or aggregating the other side to one row per customer), because joining customer_latest_order_rank (order-grain) to multi-order-per-customer data on customer_id can create duplicate order rows or inflate counts. | When composing higher-level metrics across joins, preserve correctness by ensuring joins are between compatible grains: order_id -> order-level AGG/JOINs are safe; customer-level joins require the view be reduced to one-row-per-customer (e.g., rank = 1) or the other side aggregated to order-level.

views.description: Rank orders per customer by purchase timestamp (most recent first) and expose row_rank so downstream queries can select latest N orders per customer. | Use for: Select the most recent order(s) per customer; Compute customer recency metrics; Build retention/leaky-bucket cohorts by last N orders

views.name: seller_performance_by_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  seller_id,
  COUNT(*) AS items_sold_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0)) AS seller_price_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS seller_freight_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS seller_total_value,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) / COUNT(*)) END AS seller_avg_item_value
FROM order_items
GROUP BY seller_id

params.description: Per-seller aggregated sales and value metrics computed from order_items (one row per seller_id).
params.when_to_use: Report total items sold, sums of price, freight, and total value per seller. | Compute average item value for a seller (per order_items row average). | Join seller-level financial aggregates to seller/dimension tables (one-row-per-seller) as input into further aggregations or dashboards. | Compose into higher-level aggregates (e.g., by region or account manager) by re-aggregating these per-seller metrics.
params.output_schema: seller_id: seller identifier (comes from order_items.seller_id) | items_sold_count: count of order_items rows for that seller (COUNT(*) over order_items grouped by seller_id) | seller_price_sum: sum of price for that seller (SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price, 0.0))) | seller_freight_sum: sum of freight_value for that seller (SUM(COALESCE(order_items.freight_value, 0.0))) | seller_total_value: sum of (price + freight_value) for that seller (SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price,0.0) + COALESCE(order_items.freight_value,0.0))) | seller_avg_item_value: average total value per order_items row for that seller (seller_total_value / items_sold_count, NULL if items_sold_count = 0)
params.metric: items_sold_count = COUNT(*)  -- counts rows in order_items per seller_id | seller_price_sum = SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price, 0.0)) | seller_freight_sum = SUM(COALESCE(order_items.freight_value, 0.0)) | seller_total_value = SUM(COALESCE(order_items.price,0.0) + COALESCE(order_items.freight_value,0.0)) | seller_avg_item_value = CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (seller_total_value / items_sold_count) END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to seller (dimension) tables on seller_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-seller_id, so joining to a one-row-per-seller dimension will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_enriched_times (NORM) or orders_with_customer_location (JOIN) only when you aggregate after the join. These are per-order (or per-order-enriched) datasets and may be one-to-many relative to seller_id; to avoid duplicating measures, either (a) aggregate the joined rows back to seller_id before using seller_* measures, or (b) join the seller_performance_by_order as a dimension (one-row-per-seller) on seller_id to the order-level data and use the seller aggregates as attributes (not summing them across orders). | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables/views such as order_items_by_product (AGG by product may be many products per seller) or orders_with_payments_items (JOIN with order-level or item-level rows) without re-aggregation, because such joins can multiply rows and therefore incorrectly inflate sums/counts. If you must combine, either (a) aggregate the other side to seller_id first, or (b) join on seller_id and then recompute aggregates from a base normalized table to ensure correctness. | When composing into higher-level aggregates (e.g., region totals), re-aggregate measures: sum(seller_price_sum) and sum(seller_freight_sum) are valid to compute region sums because seller_performance_by_order is one-row-per-seller. For averages across sellers, be explicit about weighting: to get average item value across sellers weighted by items, compute SUM(seller_total_value) / SUM(items_sold_count) rather than AVG(seller_avg_item_value). | This view's measures are additive over seller_id: you can safely SUM(seller_price_sum), SUM(seller_freight_sum), SUM(seller_total_value), and SUM(items_sold_count) across disjoint sets of seller_id without duplication.

views.description: Aggregate order item metrics by seller: items sold, revenue and average item value. Useful for seller ranking and performance monitoring. | Use for: Rank sellers by revenue or average item value; Identify underperforming sellers with low sales; Combine with sellers table for geographic performance

views.name: geolocation_zip_centroids
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng,
  MIN(geolocation_city) AS geolocation_city,
  MIN(geolocation_state) AS geolocation_state,
  COUNT(*) AS geolocation_points_count
FROM geolocation
GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix

params.description: Provides centroid (average latitude/longitude), representative city/state and point counts for each geolocation ZIP code prefix.
params.when_to_use: Look up the geographic centroid (lat/lng) for a ZIP code prefix to map or geocode aggregated location data. | Join geographic centroids to orders, customers, sellers or other entities keyed by geolocation_zip_code_prefix to enrich them with approximate location. | Compute ZIP-level spatial aggregates or distance calculations by using the centroid and point count as weight or metadata.
params.output_schema: geolocation_zip_code_prefix: ZIP code prefix that is the grouping key (derived from geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_prefix). | geolocation_lat: centroid latitude = AVG(geolocation.geolocation_lat) across all geolocation rows for the ZIP prefix. | geolocation_lng: centroid longitude = AVG(geolocation.geolocation_lng) across all geolocation rows for the ZIP prefix. | geolocation_city: representative city name = MIN(geolocation.geolocation_city) among rows in the ZIP prefix (used as a deterministic pick of city when multiple exist). | geolocation_state: representative state code = MIN(geolocation.geolocation_state) among rows in the ZIP prefix (used as a deterministic pick of state when multiple exist). | geolocation_points_count: number of geolocation points = COUNT(*) of geolocation rows contributing to the ZIP prefix centroid.
params.metric: geolocation_lat = AVG(geolocation.geolocation_lat)  -- average latitude per geolocation_zip_code_prefix | geolocation_lng = AVG(geolocation.geolocation_lng)  -- average longitude per geolocation_zip_code_prefix | geolocation_city = MIN(geolocation.geolocation_city)  -- deterministic representative city per ZIP prefix | geolocation_state = MIN(geolocation.geolocation_state)  -- deterministic representative state per ZIP prefix | geolocation_points_count = COUNT(*)  -- number of source geolocation rows in each ZIP prefix group
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension or lookup that is one-row-per-zip (for example, a table/view that has one row per geolocation_zip_code_prefix) on geolocation_zip_code_prefix — safe because this view is one-row-per-geolocation_zip_code_prefix and joining to another one-row-per-zip will not duplicate measures. | Do NOT join this AGG view directly to one-to-many tables/views (for example, orders, order_items, customers with multiple addresses, seller_performance_by_order, or any raw geolocation table) on geolocation_zip_code_prefix without first aggregating those one-to-many sides to one-row-per-geolocation_zip_code_prefix. Doing so would multiply geolocation_points_count and would make the centroid metrics incorrect. | If you need to enrich orders (one-to-many) with centroid info, join orders (one row per order) to this view on orders.geolocation_zip_code_prefix = geolocation_zip_centroids.geolocation_zip_code_prefix — safe because orders is one row per order and geolocation_zip_centroids is one row per ZIP; measures from this view remain at ZIP granularity and are not multiplied by orders rows in a way that distorts the ZIP-level aggregates. However, if you aggregate across orders after joining (for example SUM(geolocation_points_count) grouped by region), be aware that geolocation_points_count will sum ZIP counts across included ZIPs — this is valid only if you intended to combine ZIP-level point counts. | When composing with sibling AGG views: join only on the grouping key(s) that are equal and one-to-one (e.g., geolocation_zip_code_prefix). If the sibling AGG has a different grain (e.g., order-level), either aggregate that sibling to geolocation_zip_code_prefix first or join in a way that preserves intended semantics. | To avoid accidental duplication: prefer patterns (A) join geolocation_zip_centroids (one row per ZIP) to a fact/transaction table that is already at the desired grain and will not be further aggregated across ZIPs, or (B) pre-aggregate the fact to geolocation_zip_code_prefix and then join — this ensures the centroid and points_count remain accurate and not inflated by multiplicative joins.

views.description: Compute a representative latitude/longitude per geolocation_zip_code_prefix by averaging points. Use when joining customers/sellers by zip prefix to get approximate centroid coordinates. | Use for: Map customers/sellers by zip prefix centroid; Compute distances between zip centroids; Aggregate regional metrics by zip prefix

views.name: orders_with_customer_location
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  g.geolocation_lat,
  g.geolocation_lng
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT geolocation_zip_code_prefix, AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat, AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng
  FROM geolocation
  GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
) g ON c.customer_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix

params.description: Provides one-row-per-order with the order's customer identifiers, customer location attributes, and a centroid latitude/longitude for the customer's zip prefix.
params.when_to_use: Look up customer identity and location information for a given order_id or set of order_ids. | Enrich order-level data with customer city/state/zip and approximate geolocation (zip-code-centroid) for mapping or proximity calculations. | Compose into aggregations by order (e.g., revenue by customer city) when joined to order-level financial or item aggregations that remain at order grain.
params.output_schema: order_id: The unique identifier of the order, sourced from orders.order_id | customer_id: The customer identifier on the order, sourced from orders.customer_id | customer_unique_id: The stable customer identifier from customers.customer_unique_id (may be NULL when customer row missing) | customer_zip_code_prefix: Customer's zip code prefix from customers.customer_zip_code_prefix (used to join to geolocation centroids) | customer_city: Customer's city from customers.customer_city | customer_state: Customer's state from customers.customer_state | geolocation_lat: Average latitude (centroid) for the customer's zip code prefix, computed as AVG(geolocation.geolocation_lat) grouped by geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_prefix and exposed as geolocation_lat | geolocation_lng: Average longitude (centroid) for the customer's zip code prefix, computed as AVG(geolocation.geolocation_lng) grouped by geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_prefix and exposed as geolocation_lng
params.grounded_columns: orders.order_id | orders.customer_id | customers.customer_unique_id | customers.customer_zip_code_prefix | customers.customer_city | customers.customer_state | geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_prefix | geolocation.geolocation_lat | geolocation.geolocation_lng
params.metric: geolocation_lat = AVG(geolocation.geolocation_lat) grouped by geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_prefix (computed in the subquery) | geolocation_lng = AVG(geolocation.geolocation_lng) grouped by geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_prefix (computed in the subquery)
params.composition: Safe to join to order-level or one-row-per-order views/tables (for example: orders_enriched_times) on order_id — safe because orders_with_customer_location is one-row-per-order (grain = order_id) so joining on order_id preserves cardinality and does not duplicate its measures. | Safe to join to order-level aggregates (for example: order_payments_agg_by_order or order_items_financials) on order_id — safe because those sibling views are aggregated to the order_id grain (or documented as AGG by order) and the join is therefore one-to-one or many-to-one consistent with this view's one-row-per-order. | Safe to join to dimensions keyed by customer_id or customer_unique_id (for example: product_catalog_with_translation is unrelated; instead join to a customer-level dimension) on customer_id or customer_unique_id only if that dimension is one-row-per-customer — safe because this view contains at most one row per order and customer_id is the order's value; joining to a one-row-per-customer table will not duplicate order rows. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables/views without re-aggregation or appropriate grouping (examples of unsafe targets: order_items_by_product, orders_with_payments_items, or raw order_items) because those contain multiple rows per order. Such joins would multiply rows for the same order and thereby duplicate any order-level measures exposed by this view. Instead, aggregate the many-side first (e.g., sum amounts in order_items_by_product to order_id) and then join back on order_id. | When joining to geolocation_zip_centroids (an AGG by zip) prefer using that view instead of re-aggregating geolocation: join on customer_zip_code_prefix = geolocation_zip_code_prefix — this is safe because centroids are one-row-per-zip and will not duplicate order rows. If using the current embedded subquery, the centroid values are already computed and available on each order row. | If joining to sibling rank or windowed views (for example: customer_latest_order_rank), verify their grain — if they are one-row-per-order then joining on order_id is safe; if they are one-row-per-customer or one-row-per-order_rank, ensure the join key matches that grain to avoid accidental multiplicity.

views.description: Join orders to customer attributes and customer zip centroid (if available). Use for geographic analysis of orders at the customer level. | Use for: Analyze geographic distribution of orders; Segment orders by customer city/state or proximity; Join order-level metrics with location for mapping

views.name: order_items_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value,
  p.product_category_name
FROM order_items AS oi
LEFT JOIN product_catalog_with_translation AS p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
views.description: Denormalized order items with linked product info, seller id, order id, price and freight. One row per order_items row (one sold item). Useful as the base sales line-level table for seller-level metrics.

views.name: orders_with_timestamps_and_reviews
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  orr.order_id AS order_id,
  orr.order_approved_at AS order_approved_at,
  orr.order_delivered_carrier_date AS order_delivered_carrier_date,
  r.review_id AS review_id,
  r.review_score AS review_score
FROM order_reviews r
JOIN orders_enriched_times orr
  ON r.order_id = orr.order_id
views.description: Orders enriched with approval and carrier delivery timestamps and linked review scores (one order-review row per review). Keeps raw timestamp strings and review_score. Useful to compute packing times and order-level average review scores.

views.name: product_category_translation_map
views.description: Mapping of product_category_name to its English translation. Use to canonicalize category names for grouping and reporting.
